title: Erdos 1060 solutions to k sigma(k) equals n

problemStatement.formal: Let $f(n)$ count the solutions of $k\sigma(k)=n$, where $\sigma(k)$ is the sum-of-divisors function. Are the values of $f(n)$ bounded by $n^{o(1/\log\log n)}$, or perhaps even by a fixed power of $\log n$?
problemStatement.plain: How many integers k can have k times its divisor sum equal the same n?

Let $f(n)$ count the number of solutions to $k\sigma(k)=n$, where $\sigma(k)$ is the sum of divisors of $k$. Is it true that $f(n)\leq n^{o(\frac{1}{\log\log n})}$? Perhaps even $\leq (\log n)^{O(1)}$?



This is discussed in problem B11 of Guy's collection \cite{Gu04}.




References


[Gu04] Guy, Richard K., Unsolved problems in number theory. (2004), xviii+437.
